Every truthiness test of the field is either (a) preserve-and-append (materialize:1663,1690; assemble:1141 -- each keeps an existing note and conjoins the new one) or (b) render-only ('is there anything to quote': assemble:2010). The cap decision itself is taken from `verdict` + `producer` at assemble:1134 and inside materialize._claim_standing:1609-1644 -- never from the reason. No template/static/JS/HTML consumer exists (a repo-wide sweep over *.html/*.js/*.ts/*.j2/*.md/*.json/*.toml found only prose in docs/ and orchestration/). V5.21's finding is therefore a DOCUMENTATION defect, not a live behavioural one. Bonus: assemble:1141 is already overload-tolerant -- it runs while claim.verdict is still CONFIRMS, so it can only be conjoining a divergence note.

docstring.before:
#: non-``None`` only when a *declared* standing was capped below
    #: ``CONFIRMS`` because the backing producer was not a model.  This is how
    #: the downgrade stays visible instead of silent: the reason travels with
    #: the claim.  The cap is applied when a claim is **materialized**, never
    #: when a manifest is **read** -- a pre-existing manifest whose claim says
    #: ``CONFIRMS`` still loads (that is what ``_smoke`` witnesses); it is
    #: re-materialized once, by a later unit, after the render fix.
    verdict_reason: str | None = None
docstring.after:
#: a free-text note about this claim's *standing* or its *attribution*;
    #: ``None`` when there is nothing to record.  It carries **two distinct
    #: meanings** (U5.19 added the second), so -- stated plainly -- since U5.19
    #: a non-``None`` value does **not** imply that this claim was downgraded:
    #:
    #: 1. **cap reason** -- a *declared* standing was capped below ``CONFIRMS``
    #:    because the backing producer was not a model.  This is how the
    #:    downgrade stays visible instead of silent: the reason travels with
    #:    the claim, and ``verdict`` reads ``EXTENDS`` beside it.
    #: 2. **provenance-divergence note** (U5.19, F2) -- ``producer`` names the
    #:    *assessing* authority (a model verdict) while the material was mined
    #:    by a different producer, so the mining provenance is recorded here
    #:    beside it.  This is **attribution, not permission**: ``verdict`` may
    #:    legitimately remain ``CONFIRMS``.
    #:
    #: The two are **not mutually exclusive**: each writer *appends* rather
    #: than overwrites (``materialize._claim_for``, and
    #: ``assemble._cap_uncapped_claims``, which preserves an existing note when
    #: it caps), so one field can carry both statements ``"; "``-joined.  A
    #: consumer must therefore not read ``verdict_reason is not None`` as "this
    #: claim was downgraded" -- the authoritative downgrade signal is
    #: ``verdict`` itself.  Nor is the value structured: a clause may itself
    #: contain ``"; "`` (the divergence note does, before ``the material was
    #: mined by``), so splitting on ``"; "`` does **not** reliably recover
    #: clauses.  What *is* reliable is substring detection of the known
    #: writers: ``"capped at EXTENDS"`` is emitted by every cap site and by
    #: nothing else, and ``"is the *assessing* producer"`` by the divergence
    #: site alone.
    #:
    #: Invariant (unchanged): the cap is applied when a claim is
    #: **materialized**, never when a manifest is **read** -- a pre-existing
    #: manifest whose claim says ``CONFIRMS`` still loads (that is what
    #: ``_smoke`` witnesses); it is re-materialized once, by a later unit,
    #: after the render fix.
    verdict_reason: str | None = None
docstring.reliable_discriminator: exists: (1) the substring 'capped at EXTENDS' appears in verdict_reason iff a cap contributed -- verified emitted by ALL FOUR cap writers (materialize.py:1631, materialize.py:1641, assemble.py:1138, assess/verdicts.py:404) and by nothing else; (2) the substring 'is the *assessing* producer' appears iff the U5.19 F2 divergence note contributed -- verified emitted by materialize.py:1686 alone. NOT reliable: (a) `verdict_reason is not None` as a downgrade marker (false after U5.19 -- F2 writes a note on a claim that stays CONFIRMS); (b) splitting on '; ' to recover clauses, because the divergence clause itself contains '; ' internally ('(verdict 7); the material was mined by'), so a two-clause reason splits into three.

follow_ups.schema_typed_field: RECOMMEND a typed field, as a deliberate schema revision -- but NOT here. Proposal: `assessed_by: str` + `mined_by: str` (or a nested `provenance: {assessing, mining}` object), leaving `verdict_reason` as cap-reason text only (ideally renamed `cap_reason`). Argument: the discriminator today is SUBSTRING-MATCHING ENGLISH PROSE, which is a private implementation detail of two functions, not a contract -- and clause-parsing is impossible because a clause contains '; '. A typed field makes a consumer that must distinguish the two cases able to do so structurally. What it breaks: (a) `extra='forbid'` means a REQUIRED new field makes every existing manifest invalid -- the three real dockets (9b6a577e/445032f7/41ec711a) and every pre-U5.13 manifest would fail to load, and `_smoke` is precisely the backward-compat witness that tests this; so it must be additive-optional with a default (`assessed_by='unknown'`, `mined_by='unknown'`); (b) the schema string `resextract/docket/1` MUST NOT be bumped in this unit, so a typed field is only honest alongside a later deliberate bump to `/2` plus a reader that accepts both; (c) the writers and renderer live in docket/materialize.py and docket/assemble.py, and the tests in the five docket test files -- all outside this unit's write paths. Because a docstring cannot fix the overload and the typed field cannot be landed without a schema revision, this unit fixes the documentation and hands the type change up.

def test_guard_u523_non_none_verdict_reason_is_not_a_downgrade_marker(tmp_path):
    """U5.23: ``verdict_reason is not None`` is NOT a downgrade marker.

    The F2 note is written on a claim that legitimately stands at ``CONFIRMS``
    (a model verdict blessed replay-mined material), so a consumer must key on
    ``verdict``, not on the reason's presence.  Pins both meanings and the
    reliable discriminators.
    """
    mixed_dir = tmp_path / "mixed"
    mixed_dir.mkdir()
    db = _store_with_assessed_member(
        mixed_dir,
        state="confirmed",
        producer="replay",
        verdict="CONFIRMS",
        verdict_producer="model",
    )
    result, claims = _materialize_from_store(mixed_dir, db)
    reason = claims[0]["verdict_reason"]
    assert reason is not None                      # present ...
    assert claims[0]["verdict"] == "CONFIRMS"      # ... yet NOT a downgrade
    assert "capped at EXTENDS" not in reason       # cap discriminator
    assert "is the *assessing* producer" in reason # F2 discriminator
    assert result.manifest.generated_by.producer == "replay"
